title: Ὄνος καὶ ἀλώπηξ καὶ λέων
titleEn: The Donkey, the Fox and the Lion
part: The Donkey, the Fox and the Lion (Chambry 270)
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 270. Text as printed. Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Ὄνος καὶ ἀλώπηξ κοινωνίαν συνθέμενοι πρὸς ἀλλήλους ἐξῆλθον ἐπὶ ἄγραν.
sentences.tr: Onos kai alōpēx koinōnian synthemenoi pros allēlous exēlthon epi agran.
sentences.l: A donkey and a fox, having made a partnership with each other, went out to the hunt.
sentences.n: Fables 208 and 209 open with almost this same line, and the partnership between unequal animals is a fixed opening of the type. συντίθεμαι in the middle is to make an agreement for oneself; ἐπί with the accusative gives the object one sets out after.

sentences.t: Λέοντος δὲ περιτυχόντος αὐτοῖς, ἡ ἀλώπηξ ὁρῶσα τὸν ἐπηρτημένον κίνδυνον, προσελθοῦσα τῷ λέοντι, ὑπέσχετο παραδώσειν αὐτῷ τὸν ὄνον, ἐὰν αὐτῇ τὸ ἀκίνδυνον ἐπαγγείληται.
sentences.tr: Leontos de peritychontos autois, hē alōpēx horōsa ton epērtēmenon kindynon, proselthousa tōi leonti, hypescheto paradōsein autōi ton onon, ean autēi to akindynon epangeilētai.
sentences.l: And a lion having chanced upon them, the fox, seeing the overhanging danger, having gone up to the lion, promised to hand the donkey over to him, if he would guarantee her freedom from danger.
sentences.i: When a lion fell in with them, the fox saw the danger hanging over them, went up to him and promised to hand over the donkey, if he would guarantee her safety.
sentences.n: ἐπηρτημένον is a perfect passive participle of ἐπαρτάω: the danger is already suspended overhead and still hanging there. τὸ ἀκίνδυνον is a neuter adjective doing duty as a noun, 'the being-out-of-danger'. ἐάν with the subjunctive puts the condition as one that may still be met.

sentences.t: Τοῦ δὲ αὐτὴν ἀπολύσειν φήσαντος, προσαγαγοῦσα τὸν ὄνον εἴς τινα πάγην ἐμπεσεῖν παρεσκεύασε.
sentences.tr: Tou de autēn apolysein phēsantos, prosagagousa ton onon eis tina pagēn empesein pareskeuase.
sentences.l: And he having said that he would let her go, she, having led the donkey up, contrived that he fall into a trap.
sentences.i: When the lion said he would let her go, she led the donkey up and contrived to have him fall into a trap.
sentences.n: Another genitive absolute for the lion's answer, with the future infinitive ἀπολύσειν after φημί keeping the promise future. παρασκευάζω with an infinitive is to arrange matters so that a thing comes about.

sentences.t: Καὶ ὁ λέων ὁρῶν ἐκεῖνον φεύγειν μὴ δυνάμενον, πρῶτον τὴν ἀλώπεκα συνέλαβεν, εἶθ’ οὕτως ἐπὶ τὸν ὄνον ἐτράπη.
sentences.tr: Kai ho leōn horōn ekeinon pheugein mē dynamenon, prōton tēn alōpeka synelaben, eith’ houtōs epi ton onon etrapē.
sentences.l: And the lion, seeing that that one was not able to flee, first seized the fox, and then in this way turned to the donkey.
sentences.i: And the lion, seeing that the donkey could not get away, took the fox first, and only then turned to the donkey.
sentences.n: The donkey in the trap will keep and the fox will not, which is why the order is the whole point. ἐτράπη is the aorist passive of τρέπω used intransitively, as στραφείς is at fable 269.

sentences.t: Οὕτως οἱ τοῖς κοινωνοῖς ἐπιβουλεύοντες λανθάνουσι πολλάκις καὶ ἑαυτοὺς συναπολλύντες.
sentences.tr: Houtōs hoi tois koinōnois epibouleuontes lanthanousi pollakis kai heautous synapollyntes.
sentences.l: So those who plot against their partners often escape their own notice destroying themselves too along with them.
sentences.i: So those who plot against their partners often bring themselves down with them, and never notice they are doing it.
sentences.n: λανθάνω with a supplementary participle once more: συναπολλύντες carries the deed, and the verb says only that it went unseen. ἐπιβουλεύω takes the dative of the intended victim.
